questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. The high academic level. 
2. It was an English speaking country
3. The travel opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses/units were a bit disappointing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general fine, however, the homepage of the university was not completely updated as it stated exchange students could take some units, I could not.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction days with the needed information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I lived at Queen Mary Building. In general fine, but the hygiene was not good all the time. 
I had my own room, which was a priority for me. But also cheaper dorms where you could share a room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A big kitchen for whole the dorm (800 students)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Easy, medium pricing, you save a lot of time (and avoid stress) by not finding it yourself, the hygiene can be very poor (Depending on your luck)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find units (They call it that) at their homepage and then you apply for it through the advisor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not use the advisor about help to find units but probably possible.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Partly. I did not get some macro economics units the homepage stated was available, but I succeded in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and you will succeed in the end

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that many macroeconomics units.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was in general lower or the same. The math level expected was lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same. Lectures and classes. However, different that assignments counted toward the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Foundation in Finance
Portfolio theory and its application
Fixed Income and Securities
Environmental Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Portfolio theory and its application - Nice teacher. He made it interesting even though it is not a particular subject of interest for me. 
Fixed Income and Securities was pretty boring due to the professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The mandatory health insurance was unexpected to me. Further, some acceptance and cleaning fee for the housing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol more expensive in shops. 
Food in super market pretty much the same. 
Restaurants and cafes a bit cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Close to 150 clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I only tried the bouldring club once, but pretty clear.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ayers Rock/Uluru, road trips, the beach walks in Sydney, Melbourne, Blue Mountain (NOT SCENIC WORLD, just do the grand canyon track. Much better and way cheaper), East Coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Not that much different. Just dont be obviously drunk in the night life (Strict rules)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a mentor and talk to people in classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open-minded the first month to get some friends. 
2. Everything will work out in the end, just remember that :) 
3. Arrive the week before introduction week and settle down in Sydney.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
When going to or from the airport do not take the train to the airport station as it costs 20 AUD single trip. Instead two options: 
1. Take an Uber (pretty cheap if more people)
2. Take the train to the stop before the airport and take the bus from there. Easy way to save money.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To solve problem on my own, meet new people and the good weather. And many AMAZING travel opportunities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference, especially when it is 10 hours.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
